Header: 2026-04-15 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~45 min | Recording: ff_recording_link_8427

[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a quick QBR — usage, cost, reliability, and roadmap, then go through open actions. Priya, Jordan, you good?
[00:12] Priya Patel: Yep, all set. Maya, Rita, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Thanks, Alex. We appreciate the quarterly check-in.

Summary: Broadly positive adoption, steady increase in token usage month-over-month, a couple of latency spikes during peak hours last month tied to a third-party data transform, customer exploring Dedicated/Private for compliance and predictable tail latency.

Topics: usage trends; cost breakdown; recent incidents & mitigations; routing / caching opportunities; dedicated vs hosted discussion; next steps and roadmap alignment.

[00:45] Jordan Lee: I'll kick off with a quick usage snapshot. From March to April your token volume is up about 27%. Most of that is conversational generation routes, the summarize/agent route and the user-facing chat. Token mix shows longer tails on the summarize route which increases average context length.
[01:10] Liam O'Connor: Yeah, that's us. We rolled out the new summarization flow to 20% of users mid-March; it's heavier prompts.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: That explains it. Cost-wise you're seeing the biggest spend on the higher context routes. We've attached a per-route breakdown in the deck. There's room to optimize via prefix caching and TTL-based KV caching for the summarization use-case.
[01:40] Maya Chen: When you say KV caching, do you mean caching inferred keys? How mature is that feature?
[01:48] Jordan Lee: It's production-ready; we've seen 30-60% token reduction on similar workloads. Implementation is on the SDK side plus a small routing config — we can share example code. Apologies if I said K-V cash earlier in the notes, the auto-transcript sometimes munges KV cache.
[02:05] Rita Singh: And does that affect latency? We need to keep 95th below 450ms for the interactive UI.
[02:14] Jordan Lee: Good question. Caching usually reduces tail latencies for repeated prefixes. For cold queries latency remains unchanged, so overall 95th moves down if cache hit rate is decent. We can run a benchmark against a representative sample.

Incident review
[02:40] Priya Patel: Quick review of the April 03 outage — there was a 12-minute window of elevated errors during peak. Root cause was a downstream transform service in Kestrel's pipeline that returned malformed payloads; Redwood's routing retried and that amplified the error surface. We pushed an automatic fallback to a smaller model and triaged faster than the prior incident.
[03:10] Maya Chen: Right, our transform team introduced a schema change accidentally. We're adding stricter validation. Appreciate Redwood's auto-fallback.
[03:20] Alex Morgan: Yeah, the graceful degradation helped minimize user impact. We also noted in tracing that the KV cache was underutilized at that time because of the schema churn.

Reliability notes
[03:40] Jordan Lee: Uptime has been 99.96% this quarter from the Redwood side. Tail latency 95th for your main route averaged 520ms last month, with peaks near 820ms during a 30-minute window. For hosted customers we can implement region routing and burst reserved capacity to smooth peaks; for more predictable SLAs Dedicated with reserved GPU pools is an option.
[04:10] Liam O'Connor: Can you remind us quickly about the difference in SLA and cost for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:18] Alex Morgan: Sure. Hosted is pay-as-you-go with best-effort latency targets; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity, predictable throughput, and a contractual SLA for uptime and latency tiers. Cost is higher due to reserved GPUs, but you get predictable tail performance — helpful for UI SLAs. We can run a cost model to show break-even points based on your traffic.
[04:40] Rita Singh: We're also evaluating private deployment options because of our upcoming EEA customers and data residency needs. Any notes on the private control plane?
[04:50] Jordan Lee: Private gives you VPC or on-prem control plane variants, KMS integration for key management, and audit logs. We recently shipped additional RBAC controls and can integrate with your SSO via SAML. We'll include the network diagram and SOC2 package in the follow-up link.

[05:15] Maya Chen: On encryption — is bring-your-own-key fully supported with on-prem HSM?
[05:21] Jordan Lee: BYOK via customer KMS is supported for Private; on-prem HSM paths exist but will require scoping in the private deployment plan. We'll scope that in the next call.

Cost optimization discussion
[05:40] Jordan Lee: A few levers we recommend: 1) quantization of models for non-critical routes (LLaMA-3-variants or quantized fp16); 2) intelligent batching for high-throughput backend jobs; 3) TTL'd prefix/KV caching; 4) route-specific model selection — using a cheaper variant for low-risk outputs.
[06:05] Liam O'Connor: Do you have an estimate for quantization impact?
[06:10] Jordan Lee: In similar customers we've seen 25-40% cost reduction with minimal quality delta for summarization and classification flows. We'll run a quick A/B eval if you provide sample prompts.
[06:20] Maya Chen: We can share a small sample set. I'll pull 2k prompts to start.

Roadmap alignment
[06:30] Alex Morgan: Quick roadmap sync — over the next quarter we're rolling out: better per-token cost visibility in Console, advanced autoscaling for dedicated pools, and a network-level private deployment blueprint for EEA use cases.
[06:45] Rita Singh: The per-token visibility is huge for finance. Any ETA?
[06:50] Priya Patel: We're targeting late May for the enhanced billing dashboard, with an opt-in beta next week. We'll add Kestrel to the beta cohort if you'd like.
[06:59] Rita Singh: Yes please, put us in.

Technical deep dive request
[07:10] Maya Chen: For the tail latency, we want to run a replay benchmark against our production-like traffic. Can Jordan run that?
[07:16] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. If you can share sample traffic and a short whitelist of endpoints we'll run a 95th/99th benchmark and return the runbook with kernel selection recommendations and batching configs.
[07:28] Alex Morgan: Note — we'll need IAM-safe sample data or obfuscated payloads; don't send PII.

[07:40] Liam O'Connor: On routing, is there an easy way to route by customer tier? We want premium users on a lower-latency route.
[07:46] Jordan Lee: Yes, policy-based smart routing can route by header or token; low-latency routes map to dedicated pools in-region. There's a small config change and we can include a sample policy.

Product feedback
[08:00] Maya Chen: A small ask — the console's per-route filter is a bit slow when zooming in on 30-day windows.
[08:06] Priya Patel: Thanks, we've flagged performance for the metrics table — engineering is tracking a perf ticket.

Security & compliance
[08:18] Rita Singh: We'll need the full SOC2 package plus the audit logs retention options. Also can Redwood support a vendor risk questionnaire?
[08:26] Alex Morgan: Yes — we'll share the SOC2 attestation, network diagram, and a completed vendor questionnaire template. For audit logs we offer configurable retention windows and can export to your SIEM via syslog.

Pricing question from finance side
[08:40] Maya Chen: Any chance to get a committed discount if we move to Dedicated?
[08:45] Alex Morgan: Yes, committed monthly/annual contracts for Dedicated are priced with tiered discounts based on commit and term. We'll model that in the cost-breakdown we send.

[09:00] Jordan Lee: Quick note — we saw a pattern where some long-running generation calls weren't using cache because the client sdk had an old routing header; small SDK bump will fix it.
[09:10] Liam O'Connor: We'll push the SDK update this week.

Wrap-up and recap
[09:20] Alex Morgan: To recap: Redwood will send an updated billing + cost model, include break-even points for Dedicated; Jordan will run the latency benchmark once Maya provides sample traffic; Priya will schedule the dedicated/private scoping call; we'll include SOC2 + network docs in a secure link. Also we've added Kestrel to the billing visibility beta.
[09:40] Rita Singh: Sounds good. Appreciate the thoroughness.

[09:48] Alex Morgan: Any other questions?
[09:50] Maya Chen: No, that's it. Thanks team.
[09:55] Priya Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and the next steps.
